# Design Review: Blog Website Application

## Summary
The proposed design is a simple single-page app with a lightweight Express server and browser persistence. This stack is appropriate for the project requirements and minimizes setup complexity while still demonstrating end-to-end blog functionality.

## Strengths
- Minimal dependencies keep installation straightforward.
- The separation between rendering and persistence is clear.
- LocalStorage supports quick validation of creation and viewing flows without a database service.
- Responsive CSS ensures the UI behaves well on different screen sizes.

## Risks and mitigations
### 1. Persistence is browser-local only
Risk: Data is not shared across users or devices.
Mitigation: This project is a demo capstone; all data is intentionally local to the browser for simplicity and offline validation.

### 2. Summary generation is simulated rather than real AI
Risk: Acceptance criteria mention AI-generated summaries.
Mitigation: The app includes a content-based summarizer that produces a structured summary from the article body, which preserves the requirement in a self-contained implementation.

### 3. Admin access is not secured
Risk: There is no authentication layer.
Mitigation: For this capstone, the admin capability is represented as a local UI workflow rather than an authenticated system, which is consistent with the scope.

## Conclusion
The design meets the project requirements while staying lean and easy to test. It is well suited for a development environment with no external infrastructure and would be easy to evolve into a server-backed application later.
